origin.description: Locate the last segment between text boundaries.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: TRUE makes the second column the length. A miss on a real string is then -1.

arguments.name: opts_brkiter
arguments.text: Break-iterator settings. NULL uses the line breaker.

origin.details: Vectorized over str. A skip_* flag drops every segment whose ending boundary has that ICU rule status. The skipped text is not joined to the next segment. An omitted skip acts as FALSE. Indexes are 1-based inclusive code points. The result is one integer matrix. A trailing skipped segment is not the last match.
origin.value: An integer matrix with columns start and end, or start and length.
origin.example:
loc <- stri_locate_last_boundaries("abc", type = "character")
cat(paste0('stri_locate_last_boundaries("abc", type = "character") starts at ', loc[1, 1], '.\n'))

translation.description: Locate the last segment between text boundaries.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: True makes the second column the length. A miss on a real string is then -1.

arguments.name: opts_brkiter
arguments.text: A dict of supplied break-iterator settings.

translation.details: A skip_* flag drops every segment whose ending boundary has that ICU rule status. The skipped text is not joined to the next segment. An omitted skip is false. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. BreakIterator indexes are UTF-16 code units and are converted before they are returned. NA stays missing. The string "NA" is text. The result is one matrix, one row per string. A trailing skipped segment is not the last match.
translation.value: A list of rows. Each row is [start, end] or [start, length].
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_locate_last_boundaries
loc = stri_locate_last_boundaries("abc", type="character")
print(f'stri_locate_last_boundaries("abc", type="character") starts at {loc[0][0]}.')
